text: The two story files under 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P4 rwb-access (Access and authority)/ - RWB P4 AD016 APP Load the delegation of authority table v1.md and RWB P4 AD016 CON Load the delegation of authority table - contract v1.md - and the fragments _work/msr/fragments/RWB-P4-AD016-APP.json and RWB-P4-AD016-CON.json, all already present and written by the parallel Work Package B-P4-04 for the same two slices of legacy RWB-AD-016, stand as the deliverable of B2-P4-010: they are not rewritten, not versioned to v2 and not duplicated, and their missing values stay registered once as CG-B-P4-04-AD016-101 to -111 with ASM-B-P4-04-AD016-101 to -111. Their metadata, their 19 sections, AC1 and AC2 of RWB-AD-016 with their origin tags and the one approval-router mock Given line, the six new-under-D-RCV-60 criteria of the contract story, the four legacy test case IDs with the Level column, the nine section 12 tables and the six DP rows are kept unchanged, and B2-P4-010 registers only the duplicate-Work-Package finding.
why: The Work Package names the two story files and the two fragments as its outputs and all four already exist with complete content, because the plan issues two Work Packages for one legacy key (B-P4-04 inside a fanout and B2-P4-010 with fanout 0). Root AGENTS.md rule 1 forbids editing a file that already exists and forbids writing a path outside the Write only block, so the next-version copy that rule 1 would otherwise ask for cannot be created here, and rule 13 forbids stopping the run. The artefacts were therefore read in full, verified against Template and Rules v1 R5.3, R5.4, R5.5, R5.7, R7, R7.1, R7.2, R8.1 and R9 with the P4 context pack as the authority for service facts, and kept; the collision is recorded as CG-B2-P4-010-1 and this row, in the same way as the parallel B2-P4-005 and B2-P4-006 findings of this run.

text: The contract slice RWB-P4-AD016-CON owns no legacy acceptance criterion, because acs is empty on its line in the plan and in the Work Package, so its section 16 carries its own contract test IDs TC-AD-016-CON-01 to TC-AD-016-CON-06 at Level Contract, and the four legacy IDs TC-AD-016-01 to TC-AD-016-04 stay with the app slice RWB-P4-AD016-APP, where they test AC1, AC2, the access refusal and the forced decision-record failure. The tcs_legacy list on the contract line is therefore satisfied by ownership and not by a second copy of the four rows, and no -ITG copy is minted because no integration slice is split from this legacy key.
why: Work Package item 5 keeps the legacy test case IDs of the acceptance criteria a story owns and deviates only for an integration copy; the contract story owns none of the two legacy criteria, so restating the four IDs in its own section 16 would give one test case two owners and two Covers values.
